source.title: Cross-Modal Latent Influence: Patch-Level Training Sample Attribution for Vision-Language Models
source.authors: Laura Yao; Shi-Xing Yu; Jie Peng; Promit Ghosal; Kyra Gan; Tian-Long Chen

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present
record.tranche_reason: Tests whether learned sparse features provide useful, behaviorally consequential representations in vision-language models, an extension to a new model setting. It does not reproduce the original toy-network experiments.
record.gate_note: The study trains position-resolved SAEs on VLM activations and reports feature geometry, feature-quality measurements, and interventions on SAE latents. Those results bear on V4. Results cited from Yu et al. and other work are not counted. Curvature-estimator comparisons, modality-balancing analyses, and pooled-SAE comparisons do not directly test the listed claim versions and are omitted.
record.test_reason: MOSAIC is a training-data attribution method that uses a purpose-built SAE as a tool. Every reported result describes the authors' own SAE design: objective ablations, decorrelation that their L⊥ loss enforces, reconstruction fidelity, and influence ranking against activation ranking. None of these results bears on whether the VLMs store features in superposition or whether a dictionary recovers the model's own features. The study does not test V4 or any other version.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that MOSAIC yields localized, semantically grounded latents that preserve task behavior, and that influence-ranked latents are more behaviorally consequential than activation- or frequency-ranked ones. They also conclude that removing the image reorganizes which training examples are influential far more than it changes the latent rankings. They make no claims about superposition.
record.recipe_differences: Learns a position-resolved shared TopK SAE over task-adapted VLM activations, with spatial and phrase–region objectives and EK-FAC influence analysis; it does not use the original toy-network superposition setup or test a sparsity-dependent transition.
record.method_sensitivity: SAE placement materially affects behavior: on Gemma GQA, the fine-tuned model has accuracy 0.5914, the layer-19 SAE has 0.5867, and moving the SAE to layer 12 reduces accuracy to 0.3315 (Appendix D.3, Table 6). This is not a row for the listed versions because it measures task accuracy rather than a version's named feature property.

fits_no_version.finding: A TopK SAE (8192 latents, k=128) with spatial and alignment shaping, inserted into the VLM forward pass, roughly preserves task metrics at a mid layer. On Gemma GQA, placing it at layer 12 instead drops accuracy from 0.5914 to 0.3315.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Layer-dependent reconstruction fidelity of shaped SAEs in VLMs

fits_no_version.finding: Image and text activation-mass profiles across latents have cosine 0.73. 7,599 of 8,192 latents are active in both modalities, so the two modalities share latent directions.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Cross-modal sharing of SAE latents in VLMs

record.problems: The paper states that learned features may remain partially entangled and attribution can depend on layer and dictionary capacity. It tests only approximately 2B-parameter VLMs, and does not evaluate whether learned SAE features recover ground-truth features or remain stable across SAE training runs. Reported near-orthogonality concerns latent activity correlations, not orthogonality of decoder directions.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted for the 60-row limit. Figure-only trends across the remaining necessity/sufficiency settings are not extracted because the text gives no separate numerical values for them.

untested.parts: No toy models, no sparsity sweep, no study of geometry.
No test of capacity or importance as the cause of feature allocation.
No analysis of polysemantic neurons or their causes.
No measure of whether VLM features are spread across neurons. No test of whether SAE latents recover the model's own features rather than features shaped by the added objectives.
No test of completeness, stability across seeds, or canonicity.
No comparison of one-dimensional and multidimensional features.

record.verdict_notes: The reader linked all rows to V4. Those rows describe the study's own SAE objectives: decorrelation is enforced by a loss, and footprint changes come from the structured-sparsity loss. They do not show that features exist in superposition in the model. The study is reclassified as T4 / uses_without_test with no verdicts.

versions.untested_parts: No toy networks, feature-sparsity sweep, superposition transition, or regular geometry across sparsity levels.
Does not test whether feature importance and capacity competition determine dedicated versus shared dimensions.
Does not test alternative causes of polysemantic neurons or whether polysemanticity occurs without capacity pressure.
Tests learned sparse SAE features in VLMs, not whether naturally occurring features are spread across neurons or whether SAE features recover ground-truth model features.
Does not establish that SAE features are complete, stable across training or settings, or canonical units.
Does not compare one-dimensional feature directions with multidimensional feature subspaces.

rows.subject: Qwen3-VL-2B-Instruct
rows.operation_detail: Compared near-orthogonal feature-pair fraction before and after SAE encoding.
rows.note: The paper describes the SAE codes as substantially less correlated; this measures latent activity correlations, not orthogonality of the decoder directions.
rows.check: Measures correlation of SAE latent activity, which the study's explicit decorrelation loss (L⊥) is built to produce. This is the method's own design property, not evidence of superposition or of recovered model features.

rows.subject: Qwen3-VL-2B-Instruct
rows.operation_detail: Compared mean absolute off-diagonal correlation before and after SAE encoding.
rows.note: Measures correlation between latent coordinates, not decoder-dictionary orthogonality.
rows.check: Same issue as r1: off-diagonal latent correlation is driven by the decorrelation objective. The authors state this is not decoder orthogonality.

rows.subject: Qwen3-VL-2B-Instruct
rows.operation_detail: Measured visual footprint for the reconstruction-only Base SAE.
rows.measure: Visual footprint (fraction of image patches occupied)
rows.note: The paper defines lower footprint as more localized, but this single comparison row does not itself test a listed claim about natural model features.
rows.check: Baseline footprint of the Base SAE in the method's objective ablation. This is a comparator, not a claim result.

rows.measure: Visual footprint (fraction of image patches occupied)
rows.note: The paper interprets the decrease as more localized visual support.
rows.check: Objective-ablation result for the study's own method (structured-sparsity loss). It does not bear on natural model features.

rows.note: The authors state that alignment improves MS Lift; this footprint measure is higher than the Base SAE value.
rows.check: Objective-ablation result for the study's own method. 'Reversed' is not meaningful against any version.

rows.subject: Qwen3-VL-2B-Instruct

rows.measure: Visual footprint (fraction of image patches occupied)
rows.note: The paper reports the strongest overall representation for the combined objectives.
rows.check: Full-method footprint against Base SAE. This is the study's own method compared with its ablation.

rows.subject: Gemma-4-E2B-it
rows.operation_detail: Removed the top 256 latents ranked by influence; compared prediction flips with activation-ranked removal.
rows.note: The authors report that influence-ranked latents cause substantially larger prediction changes.
rows.check: Compares influence-based ranking with activation-based ranking. This is the method compared with alternatives, not a superposition measure.

rows.check: Task-metric preservation after inserting the study's shaped SAE. This is method fidelity, not a test of whether sparse features exist in the model.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: The tested SAE representations and interventions on Qwen3-VL-2B-Instruct and Gemma-4-E2B-it
reader_labels.reason: SAE encoding sharply reduces latent activity correlations on Qwen, and removing influence-ranked latents has a larger behavioral effect than activation-ranked removal; SAE insertion also largely preserves task metrics (r1-r4, r9-r15).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: The tested feature-localization objective ablation on VizWiz with Qwen
reader_labels.reason: The alignment-only variant has a higher visual footprint than the Base SAE, while the combined objective and structured-sparsity variant reduce it (r5-r8).
